d: Learn how to implement a rate limit for any text field that might be used by players to conduct a conversation.
h:
This example shows how to implement a rate limit of 1 minute on a text input field that allows players to post notes to a community bulletin board.

Add the following to a Script in ServerScriptService:

Server

local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")

-- Create RemoteEvent for communication
local postNoteEvent = Instance.new("RemoteEvent")
postNoteEvent.Name = "PostNoteEvent"
postNoteEvent.Parent = ReplicatedStorage

-- Rate limit of one note per minute per player
local COOLDOWN_TIME = 60 -- Time in seconds
local lastPostTime = {}

local function canPlayerPost(player)
    local userId = player.UserId
    local currentTime = tick()

    if lastPostTime[userId] then
        local timeSinceLastPost = currentTime - lastPostTime[userId]
        if timeSinceLastPost < COOLDOWN_TIME then
            return false, COOLDOWN_TIME - timeSinceLastPost
        end
    end

    return true, 0
end

-- Handle post requests with rate limit and text filtering
postNoteEvent.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, noteData)
    local canPost, cooldown = canPlayerPost(player)

    if not canPost then
        postNoteEvent:FireClient(player, "cooldown", math.ceil(cooldown))
        return
    end

    -- All text shared publicly must go through a text filter
    local filterResult = getFilterResult(noteData.text, player.UserId)
    if filterResult then
        local success, filteredText = pcall(function()
        return filterResult:GetNonChatStringForBroadcastAsync()
    end)

    if success then
        -- Create the note
        local note = {
            text = filteredText
        }
        -- Update last post time
        lastPostTime[player.UserId] = tick()

        -- Send success response
        postNoteEvent:FireClient(player, "success", note)

        -- Broadcast new note to all players
        postNoteEvent:FireAllClients("newNote", note)
    else
        warn("Error filtering text!")
    end
end)

-- Clean up when player leaves
Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player)
    lastPostTime[player.UserId] = nil
end)

kid.simple: If players can type text that others will see, like notes on a bulletin board, you need a speed limit so it does not turn into a second chat. This example lets each player post only one note per minute. It also runs every note through Roblox's text filter before anyone else sees it. The server keeps track of when each player last posted.
kid.analogy: It is like a cookie jar rule: you can take one cookie, then you have to wait a full minute before taking another.
keyPoints: Text boxes that others can read, like signs and boards, need a rate limit of at least 1 minute.
The server creates a `RemoteEvent` so clients can ask to post a note.
A table `lastPostTime` remembers when each player (by `UserId`) last posted.
If less than 60 seconds have passed, the server tells the player how many seconds are left and does not post.
All public text must go through Roblox's text filter before being shown to others.
When a player leaves, remove their entry from the table to keep it clean.

terms.rate limit: A rule for how often something can happen. Here: one note per 60 seconds per player.
terms.cooldown: The waiting time after an action before you can do it again. If you posted 20 seconds ago, your cooldown has 40 seconds left.
terms.RemoteEvent: A messenger that lets a client script and the server script send each other signals.
terms.text filter: Roblox's system that hides inappropriate words. Any text other players can see must go through it.
terms.broadcast: Sending something to everyone. `GetNonChatStringForBroadcastAsync` gets filtered text that is safe to show to all players.
terms.UserId: The unique number for each Roblox account. It never changes, even if the player changes their name.

example.title: One filtered note per minute
example.code:
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local TextService = game:GetService("TextService")

local postNoteEvent = Instance.new("RemoteEvent")
postNoteEvent.Name = "PostNoteEvent"
postNoteEvent.Parent = ReplicatedStorage

local COOLDOWN_TIME = 60 -- seconds
local lastPostTime = {} -- UserId -> time of last post

postNoteEvent.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, text)
	if typeof(text) ~= "string" or #text == 0 then
		return
	end

	-- Check the cooldown
	local now = os.clock()
	local last = lastPostTime[player.UserId]
	if last and now - last < COOLDOWN_TIME then
		local secondsLeft = math.ceil(COOLDOWN_TIME - (now - last))
		postNoteEvent:FireClient(player, "cooldown", secondsLeft)
		return
	end

	-- Filter the text before anyone else sees it
	local success, filtered = pcall(function()
		local result = TextService:FilterStringAsync(text, player.UserId)
		return result:GetNonChatStringForBroadcastAsync()
	end)
	if not success then
		warn("Error filtering text!")
		return
	end

	lastPostTime[player.UserId] = now
	postNoteEvent:FireAllClients("newNote", filtered)
end)

-- Forget players who leave
Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player)
	lastPostTime[player.UserId] = nil
end)
explain: The server makes a `RemoteEvent` in ReplicatedStorage so clients can send notes.
When a note arrives, we first make sure it is real, non-empty text.
We compare the current time to the player's last post time. If under 60 seconds, we send back the seconds left and stop.
We filter the text with `TextService:FilterStringAsync` and get the version safe for everyone.
We save the new post time and send the filtered note to all players.
When a player leaves, we remove their saved time.

watchOut: Doing the cooldown check only on the client. Exploiters can skip client code, so always check on the server.
Showing text to others without filtering it. This breaks Roblox rules.
Updating `lastPostTime` before filtering succeeds. If filtering fails, the player would be stuck waiting for nothing.
